panels.rationale: Single sagittal abdominopelvic CT from Bartholin abscess case report; caption explicitly attributes low-density fluid tracking to Bartholin's abscess, supporting bartholin_gland_disease with abscess finding; fistulous extension to rectum is rare/atypical complication.

panels.figure_caption: Sagittal image of abdominopelvic CT Showing low-density fluid tracking posteriorly and superiorly from a Bartholin's abscess, along the right side of the distal rectum and anal verge.
in_text_mentions: ellulitis of the right vulva. Finally, CT imaging showed circumferential wall thickening of the lower rectum and anus with fluid tracking posteriorly and superiorly from the Bartholin abscess along the right side of the distal rectum and anal verge (Figure 1). Though no clear communication with the anorectal lumen was seen, the reporting radiologist noted that a fistula cannot be excluded, as the lower rectum and anus were collapsed. Given the patient's reported rectal pain and purulent discharge from the patient's anus, these CT findings raise a strong suspicion for a recto-Bartholin fistula.
